description: Correspondence, addresses, letterbook, military records, family papers, genealogical chart, printed matter, newspaper clippings, and other papers relating chiefly to Indian campaigns and affairs, the War of 1812 in the Northwest Territory, slavery, and Harrison's unsuccessful 1836 presidential campaign as Whig Party candidate.  Includes a chronology of Harrison's life by his biographer, Freeman Cleaves.  Correspondents include John Armstrong, William Eustis, Duff Green, John Johnston, Joel Leftwich, Duncan McArthur, Return Jonathan Meigs, James Monroe, John Payne, William Cortenus Schenck, Isaac Shelby, John W. Taylor, Edward White Tupper, James Wilkinson, S. Williams, James Winchester, and John Wingate.

notes: Arranged in five series.  Series 1: General Correspondence, 1734-1939; Series 2: Letterbook, 1812-1813; Series 3: Miscellany, 1812-1932; Series 4: Printed Matter, 1815-1922; and Series 5: Addition, 1793-1841.
William Henry Harrison Papers available through the Library of Congress Web site at http://hdl.loc.gov/loc.mss/collmss.ms000044
Series 1-3 and a portion of Series 4 available on microfilm, no. 11,950.
Microfilm produced from originals in the Manuscript Division. Washington, D.C. : Library of Congress Photoduplication Service, 1959.
Deposit, Mary Lord Harrison, 1916.
Converted to gift, 1933.
Other gifts, exchanges, and purchases, 1901-2013.
U. S. president, senator, representative, and army officer from Ohio.
Collection material in English.
Finding aid available in the Library of Congress Manuscript Reading Room and at http://hdl.loc.gov/loc.mss/eadmss.ms009177
Index published by the Library of Congress in 1960 available in the Library of Congress Manuscript Reading Room and on Internet.  Cataloged in record 60060012.

description: Correspondence relating primarily to negotiations for the Louisiana Purchase, the Monroe-Pinkney treaty with Great Britain (1807), the War of 1812, the purchase of Florida, South American independence, and Virginia politics; diary (1825 Feb.); account book containing memoranda and official and personal accounts (1794-1802); and other papers. Correspondents include John Adams, John Quincy Adams, John Armstrong, Joel Barlow, William Benton, James Bowdoin, John C. Calhoun, William Harris Crawford, Henry Dearborn, Thomas Erskine, George William Erving, Albert Gallatin, John Graham, Richard H. Henderson, David Humphreys, Andrew Jackson, Thomas Jefferson, Joseph Jones, Rufus King, Thomas Law, Robert R. Livingston, James Madison, John McLean, John Francis Mercer, William Pinkney, Edmund Randolph, John Randolph, Spencer Roane, C.A. Rodney, Richard Rush, John Taylor, Littleton Waller Tazewell, St. George Tucker, George Washington, and William Wirt.

notes: Arranged in five series.  Series 1: General Correspondence, 1758-1839; Series 2: Additional Correspondence, 1776-1838; Series 3: Letterbooks and Account Book, 1794-1806; Series 4: Addenda, 1778-1831; and Series 5: Oversize, 1802-1819.

Microfilm edition of Series 1-3 available, no. 12,199.

Microfilm of originals in private hands. Washington, D.C. : Library of Congress Photoduplication Service, 1952.
